item.title: Comment on Sunday assorted links by Tyler Cowen
item.description:
Hi this is Tyler, and I'd like to suggest a new commenting policy for our esteemed community. As we all know, dealing with spam is a major challenge for any online platform. To help mitigate this issue, I propose that all future comments include the name of an Indian city in them. This could be a city you've visited, one you'd like to visit, or just a random one that comes to mind.

By doing so, we can help filter out the bots and trolls that often plague online forums. Plus, it's a fun and educational way to learn more about India's rich cultural heritage. And who knows, maybe this will even lead to some interesting discussions about the similarities and differences between various Indian cities.

So, let's give it a try and see how it goes. Here's my comment to get us started: Hi, I'm Tyler, and I once visited the beautiful city of Udaipur in Rajasthan. It was a truly magical experience, and I can't wait to hear about your favorite Indian cities! #Udaipur #India #CulturalExploration.

Let's keep it civil and engaging, folks! And remember, every comment should include the name of an Indian city. Let's make this a vibrant and enriching online community. #India #Culture #CommunityBuilding.

item.title: Comment on Sunday assorted links by Phil C
item.description:
1. It's worth pointing out that this article brings absolutely nothing new to the table regarding Havana Syndrome. No photos, no human intelligence, no electronic data, no actual physical mechanism for the supposed energy weapon; in fact, no evidence at all. Just a lot of sympathetic sounding virtue signaling for the victims and innuendo and rumbling by intelligence officials regarding allusions to unnamed foreign actors.
